title: A Pilot Prospective, Multi-Center Study to Monitor Time-Dependent Changes in the Thickness of Masseter Muscle After Treatment with Nabota® in Patients with Masseter Muscle Hypertrophy
content: We conducted this trial to monitor time-dependent changes in the thickness of masseter muscle after treatment with Nabota® (Daewoong Pharmaceutical, Seoul, Korea) in Korean patients with masseter hypertrophy. The current study was conducted in a series of the patients with masseter hypertrophy who visited our hospitals between January 1, 2021 and December 31, 2022. To measure the thickness of the masseter muscle, its anterior and posterior borders were determined when the patients clenched their teeth. The midpoint of the masseter muscle was determined by drawing a line connecting between the earlobe and the mouth corner. This was followed by placement of an ultrasound probe on the skin. The patients were regularly followed up weekly for 15 weeks. At each visit, they were evaluated for the thickness of the masseter muscle both at rest (resting phase) and maximum contraction (clenching phase). A total of 35 Korean women with masseter hypertrophy participated in the current study, whose mean age was 31.7±5.8 years old. All the patients were evaluated at a 15- or 25-week follow-up. There was a significant decrease in the thickness of masseter muscle at 15 weeks from baseline in the clenching phase (14.62±1.09 mm versus 9.89±1.09 mm; P< 0.05). Moreover, there was also a significant decrease in the thickness of masseter muscle at 15 weeks from baseline in the resting phase (12.45±0.57 mm versus 9.33±0.83 mm; P< 0.05). There were no treatment-emergent adverse events or serious adverse events. Nabota® might be effective in decreasing the thickness of masseter muscle in a cohort of Korean patients with masseter hypertrophy.
